public_rationale: OpenAI disclosed a $10 billion annualized revenue rate in June 2025. The full post explicitly identifies that measure before the quoted sentence, so the financial claim matches contemporaneous reporting. This supports the stated current revenue scale, not a permanent revenue ceiling or the surrounding judgments about the company.
limitations: The figure was company-reported through news outlets, with no audit status supplied.
It excludes Microsoft licensing revenue and large one-time deals.
Annualized revenue is not realized full-year revenue.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI is an unstable monolith with a vague product that can only make $10 billion a year in revenue, not profit.

statement.excerpt: The most prominent company in the tech industry is an unstable monolith with a vague product that can only make $10 billion a year (revenue, not profit) as the very fabric of its existence is shoved down the throat of every executive in the world at once.

from_speaker: Earlier in the same post: $10 billion in annualized revenue
our_interpretation: The full post explicitly identifies this figure as annualized revenue and links to reporting of the company's disclosure.
The claim therefore describes OpenAI's current revenue run rate, not realized full-year revenue or a permanent ceiling on future revenue.
June 2025 is the observation period for the current revenue rate; the sentence supplies no separate reporting period.
Unstable monolith and vague product are evaluative descriptions outside the financial test.
Revenue, not profit identifies the measure; it does not by itself assert a particular net-loss figure.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous reporting of OpenAI's own disclosure places its annualized revenue run rate at approximately US$10 billion in June 2025.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence places that June annualized revenue measure materially above or below US$10 billion.
